To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the power of the largest corporations is increasing in the U.S.; 2) the power of large corporations is exercised in a way that is not transparently accountable; 3) there is a strong relationship between the power of large firms and the lack of transparency in the exercise of that power; 4) there is no relationship between the power that corporations exercise and the legitimacy of that power; and 5) the power of corporations is exercised in ways that are not consistent with
the power of corporations is exercised in a way that is illegitimate and that this illegitimacy is not recognized by most people, including most economists.
the power of large corporations is not legitimately exercised, but it can be, and the path to legitimacy is to increase the transparency of the exercise of power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exercise of power in corporate governance and its legitimacy.
the legitimacy of corporate power.
the exercise of power and its legitimacy in the corporate sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power of corporations, and of the corporate elite, is illegitimate, and that the legitimacy of corporate governance can only be established by the convergence of heterodox economics.
power is exercised legitimately when the rules and norms that define it and its deployment are themselves legitimate.
corporate power is illegitimate to the degree that it operates outside the bounds of the rules and norms of the dominant system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

corporate governance is the set of rules, norms, and practices that govern how corporations are run, and that the legitimacy of corporate power is the degree to which corporate governance is transparent and accountable to the public.
we argue that the exercise of corporate power is not legitimate because it is not transparently exercised and, therefore, not accountable.
the legitimacy of corporate power in our society is in serious question.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exercise of power by large corporations is illegitimate because the information that would be required to hold them accountable is not available.
the exercise of corporate power is not legitimate when the information available to the public is inadequate to assess the legitimacy of the exercise.
there are many ways in which corporate governance may fail in the legitimacy test.
